Hey, it’s completely normal to feel this way in the first month. You’re still adjusting mentally, technically, and emotionally.
Give yourself some grace. Most people only look confident early on; they’re struggling just as much behind the scenes.
During my onboarding, I thought I made a huge mistake joining this company. But after 2 months, everything started making sense slowly.
They Post Jobs, You Get Ghosted.
These companies are well aware of art of ghosting😂😂
if a company isn’t ready to hire that role, fine ... but just say so.
No if no but Manager's chamcha will always win!!
Soon PM modi will also be out of the office because of AI

not seen anyone removed from the postion because of AI but yes, if someone left the team, we are hardly getting any replacements, the leadership is stating we will use AI to share the workload. Bullshit

See, whoever you are, if you keep working hard you will be rewarded sooner or later.
You are lot better than me. I never crossed 60% in my academics, had compartment in 12th, completed 4 years degree in 7 years, then left the first job in 5 months, then I was jobless for 7 years.
My father left us when I was 8 yrs old. My mom was only earner and took care of me n my sibling. She wanted me to crack govt exam, I gave those but 6 times I missed mains of Banking/railway/ssc by only 1 marks.... na giveup karte ban raha tha na continue, roz life end karne ka man hota tha. When I crossed age eligibility criteria, I was 30 years old with only 5 months of work experience. I wanted to do a lot for my mom but was not able to... Not an excuse, but there were not much opportunity in my area...chhoti moti part time jobs hi milti thi that too without PF, ya offer letter, ya salary slip and cash me salary. Ya to power sector me job thi , wo bhi netaon ke reference se ya jugad se ya paisa khila ke milti thi, ya private banks ya fir govt exam prepare karo. Gate me itne number nahi aa rahe the ki dhang ka college mile , and I haven't had money to waste on useless degree from tier 3 institute again and then search same jobs again.
During this tough jobless phase of 7 years, in last 3 years only I learnt coding, and ML. Iske pahle I haven't even touched laptop. Engg me 1 sem me bas computer subject tha that too practical only. So I started freelancing in 2017. Have done it till 2020.... Still there was no continuity in income.
With these new skillset different from my academics, I got my first job for 3.5 LPA in 2020, switched and got 9.5 LPA, switched and got 16.5 LPA, then served 3 years in a company with 2 promotions, and now I am at 45 LPA in a product company which everyone knows...and here also everything going good now
I even got chance to give interviews of Nvidia, Google, Amazon, Autodesk etc but failed to crack, but will crack definitely in future. Ye bhi crack kar leta to shayad aur better position me hota. Only regret I had that I lost my mom during covid. Ye mehnat pahle kar leta to unko khushi hoti.
When a loser like me can change things to aap to merese better ho. And India me to nahi, but I have made friends in US and other countries, wo log 35-40 ki age tak medical/accounting etc field me the still they are working at Google, Nvidia in AI field. So these people were my motivation ki jab non tech background ka doctor/accountant bina relevant degree bigtech me kaam kar sakta hai to mai to Engineer hu...mai bhi kar hi lunga.
So mehnat karte raho bro, ho jayega sab thik ya fir itne skilled ho jaoge ki khud ka kuchh start kar sako.
All the best!!👍
Subham, your story is real and relatable. Don't let the fear win, you've got this! Keep pushing and trust your gut.
